title: Regional style differences and King Oliver's Kansas City band
summary: Goodwin says Black bands sounded alike across the country, and recalls King Oliver trying to start a band in Kansas City.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Now Crook, I'd like to go on. Now we've got the difference of black and white musicians but what was greater, the difference between white bands and black bands or the difference between a Kansas City band, black or white, -- well let's say a Kansas City black band and a band elsewhere in the country?

Were the differences between two black bands greater who were playing in different parts of the country or were they greater between a black band and a white band? That's the way this question is; here at home, for example.
Or was the black style throughout the United States?
In other words, if you went to Los Angeles and heard a black band, then you would play more closely to them then you would to a white band in Kansas City?

Yeah, because you can take it that a black musician would travel from here to New York and he would travel from here to Los Angeles and vice versa. They would come from Los Angeles here. They would come through, a lot of them, but a lot of them would stay. Now why they would trade the West Coast for Kansas City or why they would trade the East Coast for Kansas City, the only thing that I could think about it would be that there had to be something here that they wanted.

There had to be something in Kansas City that these musicians wanted. I remember that the great King Oliver was here and this was on his waning days. The days he Betsy was going out, but he did try to establish a band here. It was a band of seven or eight pieces he tried to start here back in the late '30s, and I don't think it was too successful, for the fact that I don't think he got the bookings that he wanted, you know.
-- and that must have been after his New York trip, coming back probably on his way to New Orleans?
Well, I think to summarize -- Baby, did you have anything to say on this?

WELL to summarize on this question then, the difference between black and white musicians was probably greater than the difference between a band in one part of the country, black, and a black band 3,000 miles away. In other words --
